title: RT-DETR-R34 vs YOLOX-L: benchmark on one protocol
dek: On the same COCO protocol YOLOX-L leads RT-DETR-R34 by 3.2 mAP points, yet RT-DETR-R34 is faster on every runtime except PyTorch.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: YOLOX-L is the more accurate detector: 55.4 vs 52.2 mAP@50-95 against RT-DETR-R34 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, both at 640 px. It also edges the PyTorch speed test, 42.8 vs 40.2 FPS. That speed result does not travel: RT-DETR-R34 is faster on ONNX Runtime, both TensorRT builds, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5. RT-DETR-R34 also uses far less peak VRAM, 213 vs 307 MB.

RT-DETR-R34 (31.44M parameters) and YOLOX-L (54.21M) both evaluate at 640 px on COCO val2017, and both ship under Apache-2.0. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5, across four runtimes, so this comparison covers the targets where the answer changes.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. RT-DETR-R34 and YOLOX-L highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. YOLOX-L measures 55.4 mAP@50-95 to RT-DETR-R34's 52.2, a 3.2 point gap that holds across runtimes. YOLOX-L also leads on small objects: 39.0 vs 34.9 mAP_small, a 10.48% relative gap. It carries this with more than half again the parameter count.

In PyTorch on the RTX 5070 Ti, YOLOX-L runs 42.8 FPS to RT-DETR-R34's 40.2. Convert either model and the order reverses. On TensorRT FP32, RT-DETR-R34 reaches 98.1 FPS to YOLOX-L's 61.8. On ONNX Runtime it is 77.7 vs 50.6, and on TensorRT FP16 it is 108.4 vs 79.2.
The PyTorch speed result is the exception, not the rule. RT-DETR-R34 is the faster model on every other runtime and on both edge devices: 8.0 vs 5.8 FPS on Jetson Orin, 0.6 vs 0.4 on Raspberry Pi 5.

Pick YOLOX-L when you deploy in PyTorch or need the accuracy edge, especially on small objects. Pick RT-DETR-R34 for any converted runtime or edge target, where it runs faster on fewer parameters and less than half the VRAM. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the choice.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRr34.pt")  # 31.44M params, 52.2 mAP@50-95
yolox = LibreYOLO("LibreYOLOXl.pt")      # 54.21M params, 55.4 mAP@50-95

results = yolox("image.jpg")
